questions.q: What does FSCD stand for?
questions.reason: FSCD = Financial Services Collections and Disbursements: money coming in and money going out of the insurer.

questions.q: Which system calculates the premium amount?
questions.reason: The policy system decides how much the premium is. FSCD bills, collects and records it, but never calculates it.

questions.q: FSCD is built on top of which SAP engine?
questions.reason: FSCD adds insurance features on top of FI-CA, the SAP engine for millions of small, repeating payments.

questions.q: FSCD is a sub-ledger. What does it send to the general ledger?
questions.reason: FSCD keeps the detail per customer and sends daily totals to FI-GL.

questions.q: What is a Business Partner (BP)?
options: Any person or company the insurer deals with
questions.reason: Mette, Lars the agent and the garage are all Business Partners: one record, used everywhere.

questions.q: What is a contract account?
options: The customer's 'money account' (wallet) at the insurer
A list of all policies in the company
The general ledger account for premiums
questions.reason: All bills and payments for the customer land in the contract account, which also holds rules like the payment method.

questions.q: What is a posting document?
options: A permanent record of one money event
A letter sent to the customer
A draft that can be deleted
questions.reason: Every time money is owed, paid, refunded or charged, FSCD creates a numbered posting document.

questions.q: What is an open item?
options: A line that is not settled yet
A line that is fully paid
questions.reason: Open means still waiting for money (or waiting to be paid out). After payment it becomes a cleared item.

questions.q: What does 'clearing' mean?
options: Matching a payment to a bill so both are closed
questions.reason: Clearing ticks off the bill because a payment matched it.

questions.q: What do main and sub transactions tell you?
options: What kind of money a line is, which decides the ledger account
questions.reason: Example: 6100/0010 net premium and 6100/0020 insurance tax. Accounting uses them to choose ledger accounts.

questions.q: Mette's direct debit bounced. What does FSCD do?
options: Re-opens the bill and may add a fee
Nothing; the money is assumed paid
questions.reason: A return undoes the clearing so the item is open again, and in our example a DKK 100 fee is added.

questions.q: What is dunning?
options: The step-by-step reminder process for overdue money
Sending daily totals to the ledger
questions.reason: Each dunning level is stronger than the last: email/SMS, then a letter in e-Boks, then a 'cover will stop' notice.

questions.q: A premium was posted twice by mistake. What is the correct fix?
options: Reverse the duplicate with an opposite document
Ask the bank to fix it
questions.reason: Mistakes are never deleted in FSCD. A reversal creates a new document with opposite amounts; both stay visible.

questions.q: Which transaction shows a customer's whole account balance?
questions.reason: FPL9 (Account Balance) lists every line from every posting document. Start every investigation here.

questions.q: Which transaction displays a single posting document?
questions.reason: FPE3 is Display Document, like screen 1 in the guide.

questions.q: Which transaction is the payment run?
questions.reason: FPY1 creates the debit files to collect premiums and the payment files to pay claims.

questions.q: What is a reconciliation key?
options: A batch label so finance can match FSCD totals with the ledger
questions.reason: Example: all premiums billed on 01.04.2026 carry key 260401-PREM-01.

questions.q: Document date vs posting date: which one decides the accounting period?
questions.reason: The posting date is when it counts in the accounts. That's why a payment booked on 04.01 counts in January.

questions.q: In the example, Mette's net premium is DKK 8,000. What is the total with 1.1% insurance tax?
questions.reason: 1.1% of 8,000 is 88, so the total is DKK 8,088.

questions.q: Mette owes DKK 8,188 and gets a DKK 25,000 claim. With offsetting, how much is paid to her?
questions.reason: Offsetting uses the claim to pay her debt first: 25,000 - 8,188 = 16,812.

questions.q: Lars earns 10% commission on DKK 8,000 net premium. How much?
questions.reason: Commission is usually on net premium: 10% of 8,000 = 800.

questions.q: A common rule for agent commission is to pay it...
options: Only after the customer's premium is received
questions.reason: In the story Mette pays on 06.05, so Lars is paid in the 10.05 commission run, not before.

questions.q: A payment arrives without a policy number. Where does it go?
options: It is cleared against a random customer
questions.reason: FSCD can't tell whose money it is, so an operations user assigns it by hand.

questions.q: What is an FKK event?
options: A hook where developers add company-specific logic
questions.reason: Events let projects add rules, like a second approver for big claims, without changing SAP's own code.

questions.q: If the policy system and FSCD disagree on whether a premium is paid, who does finance trust?
questions.reason: FSCD is the 'money truth'.

questions.q: What happens to a posting document when the customer pays?
options: It stays the same; only its lines change from Open to Cleared
It is replaced by a new bill
questions.reason: Documents are permanent. Only the status of their lines changes.
